rics.meaning: Public Debt outstanding — total central government debt, including SBN (Surat Berharga Negara, Indonesian government securities) issued domestically and externally, plus loans from multilaterals (World Bank, ADB) and bilateral creditors.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia's gross debt level rose from ~Rp 4,500T in 2019 to ~Rp 8,000T post-COVID. Domestic SBN dominates (~65% of total) — important for FX-risk insulation. Foreign holding share of SBN (~14%) is the key external-vulnerability metric — sharp drops mean foreign outflows pressuring IDR.

rics.description: Public debt as a percentage of GDP, Standardized
rics.meaning: Public debt as a percentage of GDP — the standard sustainability gauge. Published quarterly by Ministry of Finance.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia's debt/GDP rose from ~30% (pre-COVID) to ~40% (2024) — still moderate vs DM peers (90-130%) and EM peers like India (~85%) or Brazil (~85%). The State Finance Law caps gross debt at 60% of GDP. Watch debt-service-to-revenue ratio (~20%) for nearer-term fiscal stress.

rics.meaning: Public Debt, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of the gross public debt level in USD-equivalent terms.
rics.how_to_use: Use for international comparisons. Dollar-denominated framing exposes IDR depreciation effects on foreign-currency portion. Domestic analysts use IDR-level (aIDPDEBTA) for trend analysis.
